evidence.notes: Second run, against the revised skill. Reproduced the denial with a red test and read the denial code: signature-invalid, not a constraint violation. The gateway rebuilt the verified argument map from recipient and amount only, so a holder signing over memo failed proof-of-possession before constraints ran; the triage note cites the verification order in the crate source and classifies the cause as a caller/boundary bug. Fix: memo becomes a parameter of execute_transfer and enters the single args map used for both PoP and constraint checking, is recorded by the effect, and is named with Wildcard in transfer_constraints so closed-world admits it. Recipient and amount are per-warrant parameters via the existing helper; no widening. Trusted root, clock tolerance, revocation mode, closed-world mode, TTL, depth unchanged; residual risk of untrusted free text stated. Compared with the first run, the diagnosis is deeper (PoP mismatch rather than the constraint check) and the wildcard is justified by the effect recording the value.
